- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for downward surprise.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 85% of prior peak or adjust downward 3–5% for next period.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5–10% from recent peak), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 3–7% for 2–3 periods ahead.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–3% downward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model may misread trend; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
